subject: BrightByte renewal — stability assessment and commit audit
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah@brightbyte.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightByte Finance <finance@brightbyte.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: Renewal discussion: usage spike and impact on forecast

Hi David,

We're preparing our renewal window and noticed a ~35% token usage spike in September/October tied to an internal POC. Our CFO wants a concise view of whether that usage is likely to continue and whether we should expect an ARR upsell or elevated unit cost that could change our renewal commitment. Renewal is at the end of January.

Can your team provide a forecasted ARR range (conservative / base / upside), any churn signals you've flagged on our account (support tickets, latency incidents, SLA breaches), and recommended contract guardrails (e.g., short-term holdback, staged commit)? I've attached our Q3–Q4 usage export.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — finance is aiming to finalize guidance by Nov 12.

Thanks,
Sarah Lim
Finance Ops
BrightByte

Attachments referenced: usage_report_Q3_2026.pdf
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah@brightbyte.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion: usage spike and impact on forecast

Hi Sarah — thanks for the upload and the clear ask. We've reviewed the usage export and sketched an initial renewal matrix (attached) with three scenarios and recommended guardrails. High level: the September/October spike aligns with a time-limited POC and is not yet supported by sustained traffic signals across your production routes. That pushes us to treat the current ARR as base + optional upsell rather than guaranteed.

I've attached "BrightByte_renewal_matrix_v3.xlsx" with:
- conservative, base, upside ARR projections (12-mo view)
- recommended commit probabilities by product bundle
- flag column for operational incidents and support escalations in the last 90 days

Action requested from Redwood: Marissa and Naomi — can you validate the commit probabilities and the churn flags? Marissa, please comment on the product usage vector (POC vs production). Naomi, please confirm financial holdback guidance and whether we should recommend a 10% holdback or a staged ACH schedule. Ben — please prepare a concise note on any support incidents that might affect renewal confidence.

Sarah — proposed next steps for BrightByte:
1) Redwood provides finalized renewal matrix and recommended guardrails by Nov 6.
2) Joint exec sync (Redwood finance + BrightByte CFO) week of Nov 15 to agree approach.
3) If holdback is used, we will draft proposed contract language and a DocuSign link in advance of the Dec commercial review.

I'll follow up internally and send the matrix update by Friday.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Customer Success (Renewals)
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: BrightByte_renewal_matrix_v3.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: BrightByte renewal — stability assessment and commit audit

David — quick validation notes below (pulling from usage and support logs):

On Nov 3, 2026 David Kim wrote:
> I've attached "BrightByte_renewal_matrix_v3.xlsx" with:
> - conservative, base, upside ARR projections (12-mo view)
> - recommended commit probabilities by product bundle

My assessment:
- Usage signal: the spike is concentrated in a single product path (inference-batch) tied to a POC that ended Oct 14. Production API keys show 11% month-over-month growth post-POC — healthy but not POC-scale.
- Churn indicators: two higher-severity tickets in Sept (latency on batch jobs) — mitigated by patch on Sept 29; no open escalations today.
- Recommended commit probability adjustments: conservative 45% (vs matrix 55%), base 70% (vs 75%), upside 95%. Apply the conservative reduction for FY-fin plans.

Operational asks for sales/CS:
1) Schedule a short runbook review with BrightByte infra to confirm post-POC traffic expectations (owner: Ben).
2) Agree on a staged commit: 60% at signature, 40% tranche after 90 days production validation.
3) Keep a 10% commercial holdback as a fallback tied to support SLAs.

I left inline comments in the matrix.

—Marissa
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah@brightbyte.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: RE: BrightByte renewal — stability assessment and commit audit (final)

Team / Sarah,

Thanks for the fast turn. Consolidating the audit and final recommendation below.

Summary (final):
- Recommended renewal posture: "Staged commit with 10% holdback."
- Financial projection (12 months): conservative ARR = $1.12M (45% commit probability), base ARR = $1.75M (70%), upside = $2.34M (95%). Numbers are in the attached matrix.
- Rationale: POC-driven spike; post-POC growth exists but not yet durable enough to justify full up-front commit. Two resolved latency incidents create a modest operational risk that supports a holdback.

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) David — schedule exec sync with BrightByte CFO for week of Nov 15 (target Nov 16).
2) Ben — runbook review with BrightByte infra and confirm no open tickets by Nov 10.
3) Marissa — finalize SLA-language we want tied to the 10% holdback and add to matrix comments by EOD Nov 6.
4) Naomi/Finance — prepare the DocuSign holdback template and initial billing schedule; target to have draft to BrightByte by Nov 9.

Sarah — if this approach looks acceptable I will start the DocuSign draft and share the HubSpot update for the renewal record (link included). If you prefer a shorter trial window instead of staged commit we can propose 30/60/90 validation tranches instead.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: BrightByte_renewal_matrix_v3.xlsx, usage_report_Q3_2026.pdf
